title: Suppressions
description: Every mutation a project has decided not to be shown again.

suppressions.description:
The decisions, in the order they were made. An empty list is valid and
means nothing has been dismissed yet.

DismissalReason.description:
Why a mutation was dismissed.

Two reasons, and the difference between them is worth keeping: one says the
mutation could not have been caught by any test, and the other says it could and
that a test for it would not be worth having. Only the second is a statement
about what the project wants.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `equivalent` — It cannot change what the program does, so no test could have caught it.
- `not_useful` — It can, and a test pinning that is not one this project wants.
- `unknown` — A reason this consumer does not know, written by a newer producer.

Suppression.description: One mutation a person has dismissed, and what they said about it.

file.description: The file the mutation changes, POSIX-style and relative to the project root.

mutant_id.description:
The identifier the mutant had when it was dismissed.

Provenance only, and never matched on: it names the run's survivor that
prompted the decision, and it stops being that mutation's identifier the
next time anything in the file changes.

note.description: Whatever the person wanted to say about it, for whoever reads this next.

original.description: The text it replaces. With `file` and `replacement`, the whole of the key.
